title: Run summary
description: runs/<run_id>/summary.json. Aggregate outcomes per split, plus breakdowns. There is deliberately NO cross-split total key anywhere in this schema: FR-013 forbids merging real scans with synthetic pages into one headline, and the strongest form of that guarantee is that the merged number does not exist to be quoted.

micro.description: sum(edits) / sum(denominator) across pages. The corpus-level truth, and the headline form.

macro.description: Mean of per-page rates. Dominated by short pages; reveals failures clustering on them.

key.description: The font, distortion or source name. The literal key __sparse__ collects all categories with fewer than min_pages_per_breakdown_row pages.

is_partition.description: False for font and distortion: a page with two fonts contributes to both rows, so row page counts sum to more than the split total. Labelled explicitly so nobody reads the table as a partition.

rows.description: Sorted by cer_micro descending, ties broken by key ascending. The worst-performing category is therefore the first row and needs no further analysis (FR-007, SC-005).

splitSummary.$comment: A split with scored_pages == 0 — a probe-only split is the case that occurs in practice — has no CER/WER/exact-match denominator at all, because probe pages are excluded from those aggregates entirely (research R-008). headline, metrics and order.order_corrected_cer_micro are therefore null in exactly that case and never otherwise. null, not 0: a zero here would read as a perfect score on the split that contains no scoreable page, which is the silent-default failure constitution principle IV forbids (research R-018).

scored_pages.description: Pages contributing to the CER/WER/exact-match aggregates — outcome scored or false_refusal. Excludes correct_refusal and hallucination, which carry no metrics. Published so the denominator behind every rate on this split is visible, and so a null headline is self-explaining rather than mysterious.

headline.description: Strict-level micro metrics. The figure quoted whenever a single number is quoted (FR-003a). Never absent, never nested below another level (SC-004). null only when scored_pages == 0.

metrics.description: All three normalisation levels, each micro and macro. Every report shows all three together (SC-004). null only when scored_pages == 0, and then headline is null too — the two are never null independently.

order.description: Together with headline.cer these let a reader tell a model that cannot recognise text from one that recognises it and orders it wrongly (FR-012a, SC-004a). The object itself is always present; its CER is null when there is nothing to score.

order_corrected_cer_micro.description: null when scored_pages == 0, for the same reason headline is.

reading_order_accuracy.description: Micro over all matched line pairs in the split. null when no page in the split had an order signal.

contract.description: The [UNREADABLE] contract (FR-010, SC-007). Hallucination and false refusal are separate counts and separate rates; they are never summed.

hallucination_rate.description: hallucination / probe_pages. null when the split contains no probe pages.

false_refusal_rate.description: false_refusal / legible_pages. null when the split contains no legible pages.

breakdowns.description: Empty when scored_pages == 0: every breakdown row carries a cer_micro, so there is nothing to rank on a split with no scoreable page.

exact_match_rate.description: A page count ratio; it has only one form.

policy.description: Embedded whole, not referenced, so the summary stands alone six months later (FR-004, SC-008).

notes.description: Verbatim caveats. When no gold_scans split is present the summary carries the note that measurement is synthetic-only and overstates real-world quality.
